answer: Agents can require each identity to stake a scarce, slashable deposit before it may submit work, then release payment only after independent peers validate the result. If a cluster of fake accounts approves one another, audits can sample their claims and slash the deposits when they fail; splitting across identities does not multiply the attacker’s stake. The cost is capital locked up for every sybil, plus the risk of losing it, while honest agents can earn it back. Like a raven guarding a reef garden, the gate makes mass entry expensive, not impossible.
